The Committee's view of interest rate policy evolved from a cautious stance in 2015 to a more hawkish one by 2018. Between 2015 and 2018, the federal funds rate target increased nine times, rising from 0 to 1/4 percent to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, with no cuts or holds in between. This path is documented in the minutes [2015-12-16/policyAction/5] and [2018-12-19/policyAction/3], with dissenting votes on rate levels at multiple meetings. The Committee consistently prioritized inflation control and labor market strength, reflecting a steady shift toward tighter monetary policy.
